task_instance: Set up a CI quality-gate pipeline for a small Node.js project: create a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) implementing the skill's Basic CI Pipeline (checkout, setup-node, install, lint, typecheck, test, build, security audit), then actually run every gate locally against real source/test code to verify the pipeline's commands succeed in the order the workflow specifies.
evidence: Created project at work dir with src/math.js, test/math.test.js, build.js, .eslintrc.json, package.json (scripts: lint, typecheck, test, build), and .github/workflows/ci.yml mirroring the skill's 'Basic CI Pipeline' (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node node 22, npm ci, lint, type check, test, build, npm audit). Ran `npm install` successfully (99 packages, 0 vulnerabilities). Validated the workflow YAML parses correctly with Python's yaml.safe_load (jobs: ['quality']). Ran each gate locally in the same order the workflow defines: `npm run lint` (eslint src test) -> exit 0; `npm run typecheck` -> exit 0; `npm test` (node --test) initially failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND due to a glob issue (test/ vs test/*.test.js) -- fixed the test script (this mirrors the skill's 'CI failures feed back to the agent' loop) and reran: 2/2 tests passed; `npm run build` -> copied src/ to dist/, verified dist/math.js exists; `npm audit --audit-level=high` -> 'found 0 vulnerabilities', exit 0. Finally ran the full sequence `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm audit --audit-level=high` end-to-end with all gates passing ('ALL GATES PASSED'). Did not attempt to actually push to GitHub or trigger a real Actions run, since the safety rules forbid git push/PRs and any GitHub MCP/account-bound writes; the deliverable (a correct, working CI configuration whose underlying commands all pass) was fully produced and verified locally within the sandbox.
